title: What is cli-fi
titleChinese: 什么是“气候变化类影视文学作品”？
paragraphs: If you could travel back in time, which period of history would you visit? It’s a great question to ask your friends, and time travel is the subject of many science fiction films. Of course, sci-fi is familiar to most of us, but what is cli-fi? The simple answer is climate fiction – a genre which focuses on the subject of climate change.

Many of the cli-fi examples we watch tend to be disaster films. It could be solar flares, ice ages devastating the planet, extreme flooding swamping the Earth with water, or super-storms that threaten life as we know it. While films and novels of this genre are often subject to the typical tropes of a hero or heroine battling to save the day, what sets it apart from most sci-fi films is that the plots will often draw on plausible outcomes in the present or near future.

Climate change and the potential threats have long been established. Some believe that the issue of climate change has even led to more fans watching films to learn more about what’s happening to the world – seeing it as a form of edutainment. A study conducted by the Yale programme on Climate Change Communication tested the effects that two climate fiction novels can have on its readers and found “significant positive effects” in terms of their attitudes and beliefs towards the climate crisis – for example, understanding global warming will harm them and future generations.

Most climate films are not only blockbuster action films, but also prey on our fear of what some see as the impending doom of a climate catastrophe. This sounds bad, but according to a study conducted on 310 adults in the US, watching scary films can help us feel more prepared, resilient and less alone in situations such as the pandemic. So, it looks like cli-fi is here to stay – and there seem to be some benefits. Whether it’s there to educate, entertain or prepare you for a climate crisis, it might have a role to play.

vocabulary.entry: genre /ˈʒɒnrə/ n. （文学、艺术的）类型，体裁
vocabulary.example: This novel belongs to the fantasy genre.
vocabulary.translation: 这部小说属于奇幻文学体裁。

vocabulary.entry: solar flare /ˈsəʊlə fleə/ n. 太阳耀斑
vocabulary.example: A powerful solar flare can disrupt satellite communications.
vocabulary.translation: 强烈的太阳耀斑会干扰卫星通信。

vocabulary.entry: devastate /ˈdevəsteɪt/ v. 彻底破坏，摧毁
vocabulary.example: The hurricane devastated the coastal towns in a single night.
vocabulary.translation: 飓风一夜之间摧毁了沿海的多个城镇。

vocabulary.entry: swamp /swɒmp/ v. 淹没，使泛滥
vocabulary.example: Heavy rains swamped the low-lying areas of the city.
vocabulary.translation: 暴雨淹没了城市的低洼地带。

vocabulary.entry: trope /trəʊp/ n. （文学艺术中的）惯用手法，套路
vocabulary.example: The "chosen one" is a common trope in fantasy stories.
vocabulary.translation: “天选之子”是奇幻故事中常见的套路。

vocabulary.entry: heroine /ˈherəʊɪn/ n. 女主人公，女英雄
vocabulary.example: The novel’s heroine is a brave young doctor working in a war zone.
vocabulary.translation: 这部小说的女主人公是一位在战区工作的勇敢年轻医生。

vocabulary.entry: battle to save the day /ˈbætl tu seɪv ðə deɪ/ 奋力扭转局面，力挽狂澜
vocabulary.example: The firefighters battled to save the day when the building caught fire.
vocabulary.translation: 大楼起火时，消防员奋力扑救，力挽狂澜。

vocabulary.entry: plausible /ˈplɔːzəbl/ adj. 看似合理的，可信的
vocabulary.example: The scientist put forward a plausible explanation for the phenomenon.
vocabulary.translation: 这位科学家为该现象提出了一个看似合理的解释。

vocabulary.entry: potential /pəˈtenʃl/ adj. 潜在的，可能的
vocabulary.example: We need to identify and address potential risks in the project.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要找出并应对项目中的潜在风险。

vocabulary.entry: edutainment /ˌedjuˈteɪnmənt/ n. 寓教于乐的内容或形式
vocabulary.example: The app combines learning and games to create perfect edutainment for kids.
vocabulary.translation: 这款应用将学习与游戏结合，为孩子打造了绝佳的寓教于乐体验。

vocabulary.entry: conduct /kənˈdʌkt/ v. 实施，进行（研究、调查等）
vocabulary.example: Researchers conducted a survey to gather public opinions on the new policy.
vocabulary.translation: 研究人员开展了一项调查，收集公众对新政策的看法。

vocabulary.entry: significant /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt/ adj. 显著的，重大的
vocabulary.example: The new discovery made a significant contribution to medical science.
vocabulary.translation: 这项新发现为医学做出了重大贡献。

vocabulary.entry: attitude /ˈætɪtjuːd/ n. 态度，看法
vocabulary.example: Her positive attitude towards life inspires everyone around her.
vocabulary.translation: 她积极的生活态度鼓舞着身边的每一个人。

vocabulary.entry: global warming /ˈɡləʊbl ˈwɔːmɪŋ/ n. 全球变暖
vocabulary.example: Global warming is causing the melting of polar ice caps.
vocabulary.translation: 全球变暖正导致极地冰盖融化。

vocabulary.entry: blockbuster /ˈblɒkbʌstə/ n. 风靡一时的作品，大片
vocabulary.example: The new superhero film is expected to be a summer blockbuster.
vocabulary.translation: 这部新的超级英雄电影有望成为暑期大片。

vocabulary.entry: prey on /preɪ ɒn/ 利用（他人的恐惧、弱点等）
vocabulary.example: Some advertisements prey on people’s fear of aging to sell skincare products.
vocabulary.translation: 一些广告利用人们对衰老的恐惧来推销护肤品。

vocabulary.entry: impending /ɪmˈpendɪŋ/ adj. 即将发生的，逼近的
vocabulary.example: Residents were warned about the impending storm and advised to stay indoors.
vocabulary.translation: 居民们收到了即将有暴风雨的预警，被建议待在室内。

vocabulary.entry: doom /duːm/ n. 厄运，劫数
vocabulary.example: The novel depicts the doom of a civilization destroyed by environmental disasters.
vocabulary.translation: 这部小说描绘了一个被环境灾难摧毁的文明的覆灭。

vocabulary.entry: catastrophe /kəˈtæstrəfi/ n. 灾难，灾祸
vocabulary.example: The oil spill was an environmental catastrophe that affected marine life for years.
vocabulary.translation: 这次石油泄漏是一场环境灾难，对海洋生物的影响持续了多年。

vocabulary.entry: resilient /rɪˈzɪliənt/ adj. 有韧性的，适应力强的
vocabulary.example: Communities that work together are more resilient in the face of natural disasters.
vocabulary.translation: 团结协作的社区在面对自然灾害时更具韧性。

vocabulary.entry: pandemic /pænˈdemɪk/ n. （全国或全球性）流行病，大流行病
vocabulary.example: The country took strict measures to control the spread of the pandemic.
vocabulary.translation: 该国采取了严格措施来控制这场大流行病的传播。

vocabulary.entry: stay /steɪ/ v. 继续存在，保持
vocabulary.example: The tradition has stayed for hundreds of years in this small village.
vocabulary.translation: 这一传统在这个小村庄已经延续了数百年。

vocabulary.entry: establish /ɪˈstæblɪʃ/ v. 确定，证实
vocabulary.example: Scientists have established a link between smoking and lung cancer.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家已经证实了吸烟与肺癌之间的关联。

vocabulary.entry: threaten /ˈθretn/ v. 威胁，危及
vocabulary.example: Pollution threatens the survival of many endangered species.
vocabulary.translation: 污染正危及许多濒危物种的生存。

vocabulary.entry: draw on /drɔː ɒn/ 利用，凭借
vocabulary.example: The author drew on her own childhood experiences to write the novel.
vocabulary.translation: 这位作者利用自己的童年经历创作了这部小说。

sentences.english: If you could travel back in time, which period of history would you visit?
sentences.chinese: 如果你能穿越回过去，你会造访哪个历史时期？

sentences.english: It’s a great question to ask your friends, and time travel is the subject of many science fiction films.
sentences.chinese: 这是一个很适合问朋友的问题，而时空旅行也是许多科幻电影的主题。

sentences.english: Of course, sci-fi is familiar to most of us, but what is cli-fi?
sentences.chinese: 当然，科幻对我们大多数人来说都不陌生，但什么是气候科幻呢？

sentences.english: The simple answer is climate fiction – a genre which focuses on the subject of climate change.
sentences.chinese: 答案很简单，就是以气候变化为主题的文学类型。

sentences.english: Many of the cli-fi examples we watch tend to be disaster films. It could be solar flares, ice ages devastating the planet, extreme flooding swamping the Earth with water, or super-storms that threaten life as we know it.
sentences.chinese: 我们看过的大多数气候科幻作品都偏向灾难片的类型，情节可能是太阳耀斑爆发、冰河时代席卷地球、特大洪水淹没万物，或是超级风暴威胁人类的生存。

sentences.english: While films and novels of this genre are often subject to the typical tropes of a hero or heroine battling to save the day, what sets it apart from most sci-fi films is that the plots will often draw on plausible outcomes in the present or near future.
sentences.chinese: 这类题材的影视和文学作品虽然也常常沿用“英雄人物力挽狂澜”的经典套路，但它与多数科幻作品的区别在于，其情节往往基于当下或不远的未来可能会真实发生的结果。

sentences.english: Climate change and the potential threats have long been established.
sentences.chinese: 气候变化及其潜在威胁早已是公认的事实。

sentences.english: Some believe that the issue of climate change has even led to more fans watching films to learn more about what’s happening to the world – seeing it as a form of edutainment.
sentences.chinese: 有人认为，正是气候变化这一议题，让更多人愿意通过观影来了解世界正在发生的变化——将这类影片视为一种兼具教育与娱乐属性的载体。

sentences.english: A study conducted by the Yale programme on Climate Change Communication tested the effects that two climate fiction novels can have on its readers and found “significant positive effects” in terms of their attitudes and beliefs towards the climate crisis – for example, understanding global warming will harm them and future generations.
sentences.chinese: 耶鲁大学气候变化传播项目曾做过一项研究，测试两本气候科幻小说对读者的影响，结果发现，这些作品对读者看待气候危机的态度和认知产生了“显著的积极作用”，比如让读者意识到全球变暖会对自身及后代造成危害。

sentences.english: Most climate films are not only blockbuster action films, but also prey on our fear of what some see as the impending doom of a climate catastrophe.
sentences.chinese: 大多数气候科幻电影不仅是卖座的动作大片，还利用了人们对气候灾难即将来临的恐惧心理。

sentences.english: This sounds bad, but according to a study conducted on 310 adults in the US, watching scary films can help us feel more prepared, resilient and less alone in situations such as the pandemic.
sentences.chinese: 这听起来似乎不是什么好事，但一项针对310名美国成年人的研究显示，观看这类惊悚影片能让我们在面对疫情这类危机时，变得更有准备、更具韧性，也不再感到孤立无援。

sentences.english: So, it looks like cli-fi is here to stay – and there seem to be some benefits.
sentences.chinese: 由此可见，气候科幻作品会一直存在，而且它确实有不少积极意义。

sentences.english: Whether it’s there to educate, entertain or prepare you for a climate crisis, it might have a role to play.
sentences.chinese: 无论其作用是科普、娱乐，还是让人们为应对气候危机做好准备，这类作品都有着自身的价值。
